question: can you explain the 3 types of worship in the table? the last one confused me
note: p55: acts of the heart (love, fear, hope, khushoo'); physical acts (prayer, zakaat, pilgrimage); acts abandoned in obedience (e.g. alcohol, adultery; food and drink while fasting).

resp.text: Through worship, a Muslim glorifies Allah and draws closer to Him. Worship includes all inward and outward words and deeds that Allah loves. A person can transform everyday habits like eating and sleeping into worship simply by having a good intention. Acts of worship include deeds of the heart, physical actions, and abstaining from forbidden things in obedience to Allah. For an act of worship to be accepted, it must be done sincerely for Allah alone and performed just as the Prophet did. These acts have different levels, from duties required of every Muslim to recommended deeds.

question: ok but do I need all that at home in front of my dad and brothers too?
history:
Learner: what are the hijab rules
Tutor: In front of men who are not related to you, cover the whole body with clothing that is loose, not see-through, and not attractive in itself.
note: p101: in front of men she cannot marry (father, son, brother) she may appear as before women, showing face, hair, neck and feet; p73 mahram.

resp.text: No, you do not need to cover your entire body in front of your father and brothers. In front of male relatives whom you are forbidden to marry, such as your father and brother, you may appear as you normally would before other women. You may show parts of your body such as your face, hair, neck, and feet. Forearms are also among the body parts that do not need to be covered before such relatives according to prevailing custom, provided it is done without excess and stays within the limits of decency.

question: I'm going to slaughter a chicken myself for the first time on my uncle's farm. How do I do it the halal way?
note: p105: slaughterer Muslim/Jew/Christian of discretion; sharp tool that makes blood flow (no stunning); say Bismillaah; cut oesophagus, throat and two jugular veins (or three of the four).

resp.text: To slaughter the halal way, you must satisfy four conditions. The person slaughtering must be a Muslim, Jew, or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out the act for the intended purpose. The tool must be sharp, suitable for the intended purpose, and cause blood to flow, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that kills the animal due to heavy weight, hits its head to death, or renders it unconscious by electric stunning. You must pronounce the name of Allah by saying Bismillaah at the time of slaughtering. Finally, you must cut the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or at least three of these four.

question: Ist es erlaubt, gebrauchte Sachen auf Kleinanzeigen zu verkaufen?
note: p108: general rule: transactions are permissible unless forbidden; p109: selling unknown things is forbidden.

resp.text:
Die allgemeine islamische Regel besagt, dass alle Arten von Transaktionen erlaubt sind und keine davon verboten ist, außer was im Koran oder in der Sunna des Propheten für verboten erklärt wurde. Verboten sind finanzielle Transaktionen unter anderem dann, wenn Dinge verkauft werden, die unbekannt sind. Ebenso ist der Handel mit Substanzen verboten, die der menschlichen Gesundheit schaden, wie etwa Alkohol, Drogen und Tabak. Auch das widerrechtliche Aneignen fremden Eigentums, wie durch Täuschung oder Zwang, ist verboten.
